message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me think through this step by step. First, I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we've had two dates so far. The first date went well, and the second date on Wednesday was also good. We planned to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie, which would have been our third date. But here's the thing: I've had an incredibly long week. I only got about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with just a half-hour break. By the time Friday rolled around, I was completely exhausted. He messaged me around 5:30 pm asking if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself. I told him I felt horrible because I was absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, and I offered to take him out for lunch and pay for it, and we could watch a movie then. I haven't heard back from him yet. Now, I'm worried that he might think I'm not interested anymore, especially since I mentioned earlier that I wanted to take things slow. I don't want him to think I'm trying to get out of the relationship or that I'm not interested. I just really needed some rest. Is it wrong to cancel a date because I'm tired? Or is it okay because I'm not feeling well? I guess I need to consider how he might feel about this. On one hand, I'm being honest about my feelings and taking care of myself. On the other hand, canceling plans might make him feel like I'm not committed or interested. Maybe I should have communicated differently. Instead of saying I was shattered, maybe I could have explained that I had a really tough week and needed some rest. Or perhaps I could have suggested a different activity that's less demanding, like just talking over coffee instead of watching a movie. I also wonder if it's better to keep the plans as they are, even if I'm tired, to show commitment. But then, if I'm not in a good state, I might not enjoy the date, and that could come across as being disinterested. Another thing to think about is whether this is a common occurrence. If I'm frequently canceling dates because I'm tired, that might be a problem. But in this case, it's just one time, and I had a valid reason. I also need to consider cultural differences. In some cultures, canceling plans is more acceptable than in others. Since I'm in Australia, I'm not sure how common it is to reschedule dates due to tiredness. Overall, I'm torn between being honest about my feelings and maintaining the relationship's momentum. I don't want him to feel like I'm pulling away, but I also don't want to pretend to be okay when I'm not. Maybe the best approach is to communicate my feelings clearly and apologize for the inconvenience. I should reassure him that I still want to spend time with him and that this was just a one-time thing due to my exhaustion. I also need to think about how I would feel if the situation were reversed. If he was tired and wanted to reschedule, would I be understanding, or would I feel like he wasn't interested? I think I would want him to be honest with me, so I should extend the same courtesy. In conclusion, while canceling a date because of tiredness might seem petty, it's important to communicate honestly and take care of yourself. Relationships require mutual understanding and respect, and being upfront about your needs can actually strengthen the relationship in the long run.
